text:
sara (Docs): opened a small PR to add a "spike 429" troubleshooting note and two lightweight SDK snippets: backoff that honors Retry-After, and a streaming retry helper that trims oldest tokens. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4973

ben (SRE): nice. does the repro cover both sudden fanout bursts and steady capacity limits? dedicated nodes behave differently.

sara (Docs): included both. TL;DR repro steps in PR: run fanout script at ~150-250 req/s for 20-40s with 30-70ms jitter to emulate many clients, capture Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* headers. For dedicated, run same load but note the Retry-After values are often proportional to capacity units.

oliver (SDK): can we make the JS streaming retry example explicit about dropping oldest messages vs summarizing? customers always ask. I'll add a comment about token accounting using our tokenizer helper.

sara (Docs): yes 1 added a short recommendation: prefer summarization for high-fidelity contexts, drop-oldest for chatty ephemeral history.

harper (Eng): operational note: streaming retries should include the partial buffer in token count when trimming, otherwise you'll resend overlapping tokens. Add a one-liner about that.

ben (SRE): adding curl repro example to PR would help support teams. e.g.:
```bash
for i in {1..400}; do curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; sleep 0.03; done
```

sara (Docs): added the curl loop and linked to runbook anchor: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/rl-429#spike-vs-capacity

oliver (SDK): pushed a tiny change to the streaming snippet: show how to compute token count and drop while count > max. JS snippet in PR: 
```js
// stream-retry-trim.js
const {tokenize} = require('@redwood/tokenizer')
function trimOldest(messages, maxTokens) {
  let total = messages.reduce((s,m)=>s+tokenize(m.text).length,0)
  while(total > maxTokens) {
    const removed = messages.shift()
    total -= tokenize(removed.text).length
  }
  return messages
}
// note: include active partial output buffer in maxTokens calculation before retry
```

oliver (SDK): also added comment that Retry-After header takes precedence over exponential backoff and that decimal seconds may appear.

sara (Docs): added a small routing policy example recommending fallback to "gptx-small" with rate-limited admission or queueing as graceful degrade. Also included a short blurb about SLA implications for customers switching fallbacks.

harper (Eng): small nit: add a one-line warning that client-side aggressive retry loops can exacerbate bursts. suggest capping concurrent retries per user token.

ci-bot: sara updated files: docs/troubleshooting/spike-429.md, snippets/stream-retry-trim.js, snippets/backoff_honor_retry_py.py

sara (Docs): request: @ben @oliver can you quick-ack so I can merge before the docs sprint cutoff? If SRE wants to tweak the dedicated repro steps, drop them here and I'll update.

ben (SRE): ack, will run the curl loop against a dedicated staging pool in the AM and post any wording changes.

oliver (SDK): ack from SDK - examples look good, thanks for the clear notes about token accounting.

sara (Docs): thanks all 1 I'll lint and merge once SRE confirms dedicated numbers.
